text_raw:
# Northfield Software Ltd — Company Overview

*Student-facing document. Part of Phase 1 release.*

## What Northfield does

Northfield Software Ltd ("Northfield") builds and sells **Northfield OS**, a scheduling, compliance-tracking and invoicing product for small and mid-sized trades and facilities-services businesses (electrical, HVAC, plumbing, commercial cleaning). Customers are typically businesses with 5–200 field staff.

Northfield sells directly (no channel/reseller layer), with a small implementation team that onboards new customers and a support team that handles ongoing issues. It is privately held, founded in 2020, and has never raised outside venture funding beyond an early seed round.

## Size and structure

- **29 employees** as of 31 July 2026.
- **Five business functions**: Leadership, Sales, Customer Success & Delivery, Engineering & Product, Finance & People Ops.
- Single office location; fully in-person with two remote engineers.

## Dataset period

The dataset covers **1 August 2025 – 31 July 2026** ("the period"). Some documents (policies, role descriptions) predate the period and remain in force; where a document has been superseded, both versions are provided, as they would be in a real organisation.

All claims, evidence and records should be read as current **as at 31 July 2026** unless a document states otherwise.

## Core business processes

The dataset is built around eight core processes. These are the backbone against which most knowledge claims are defined:

| Code | Process | Primary function(s) |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Customer discount approval | Sales, Finance |
| P2 | Customer onboarding / implementation | Customer Success & Delivery |
| P3 | Product change / feature request intake | Engineering & Product |
| P4 | Expense approval | Finance & People Ops |
| P5 | Support escalation | Customer Success & Delivery, Engineering & Product |
| P6 | New hire onboarding | Finance & People Ops (People Ops) |
| P7 | Invoicing & collections | Finance & People Ops |
| P8 | Contract renewal & churn-risk review | Sales, Customer Success & Delivery |

## Reading this dataset

This dataset is **deliberately imperfect**. It contains gaps, contradictions, outdated documents, claims supported by only one source, and areas where the organisation itself does not have a settled answer. This is intentional and is the subject of the assessment exercise — do not assume any single document is authoritative simply because it looks formal, recent, or comes from a senior person.

# Decision Rights Table

*Student-facing document. Part of Phase 1 release. A cross-role summary of who holds which decision right, per the brief's request for org chart + role descriptions + a standalone decision-rights table as three distinct artifacts. Detail and caveats for each role are in [role_descriptions.md](role_descriptions.md); this table is the quick-reference cut across roles.*

| Decision | Formal decision right (documented) | Observed in practice | Documented? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Approve discount >15% on new-business deals | Head of Finance & People Ops (POL-01) | Often Head of Sales, informally, for urgent deals | Formal right documented; practice is not |
| Approve renewal discount | Account Executive, within the 10% cap (POL-06) | Same, but at least one instance of an undocumented exception above the cap | Formal right documented; exception is not |
| Final call on renewal terms when Sales and Customer Success disagree | **Not assigned to any role** | Resolved informally case-by-case, or left unresolved | Not documented — this is a genuine gap, not an omission from this table |
| Approve expense claims >$500 | Head of Finance & People Ops (POL-07) | Sometimes pre-approved informally by the employee's manager | Formal right documented; practice is not |
| Approve a deviation from the standard 6-week onboarding timeline | **Not formally assigned** — informally treated as the Head of Customer Success & Delivery's call | Same, by habit rather than documented authority | Not documented |
| Sign off on production deployments touching customer billing | Head of Engineering (per role description) | Mostly followed; one emergency fix during the February 2026 incident has no clear sign-off record | Formal right documented; one instance ambiguous |
| Approve a new hire's completion of probation | People Ops Lead, sole approver (POL-08) | Consistently followed | Documented and followed |
| Approve/reject a discount-relevant CRM stage change | Account Executive (deal owner) | Consistently followed | Documented and followed |
| Prioritise incoming feature requests | Product Managers jointly (PROC-03) | Split informally by bandwidth/customer familiarity, no fixed rule | Formal right documented; split method is not |
| Decide technical feasibility vs. prioritisation split between Engineering and Product | **Not documented anywhere** as a formal split | Assumed/talked out case-by-case | Not documented |
| Approve escalation-process changes (e.g. the v2 draft) | Head of Customer Success & Delivery | A pilot was authorised verbally; no formal approval was ever recorded, though the team has operated as if it were approved | Ambiguous — a decision right exists, but whether it was exercised is contested |
| Block a release for a data-quality defect | **Not documented** | QA Lead has flagged issues; no confirmed instance of unilaterally blocking a release | Not documented |

**How to read this table:** the gap between "Formal decision right" and "Observed in practice" is often the point of a specific reference claim (see the hidden reference set once released) — this table exists to make those gaps visible at a glance rather than requiring a read of every role description and process document to spot them.

title: Role Descriptions and Decision Rights

# Role Descriptions and Decision Rights

*Student-facing document. Part of Phase 1 release. Covers roles most relevant to the core processes; not every role in the roster has a full description. See [decision_rights_table.md](decision_rights_table.md) for a cross-role decision-rights summary.*

## CEO — Renata Voss

- **Function:** Leadership
- **Reports to:** Board
- **Responsibilities:** Overall strategy, board relationship, final call on strategic decisions (market expansion, fundraising).
- **Decision rights:** Sole authority on strategic direction; delegates day-to-day operational authority to the COO and function heads.
- **Systems accessed:** All systems (admin access).
- **Process participation:** P7 (strategic escalations only), general oversight.
- **Backup/delegate:** COO acts with delegated authority in the CEO's absence, except for strategic decisions.

## COO — Marcus Ihejirika

- **Function:** Leadership
- **Reports to:** Renata Voss (CEO)
- **Responsibilities:** Operational oversight across Customer Success & Delivery, cross-functional coordination.
- **Decision rights:** Formal line management of Head of Customer Success & Delivery. In practice, day-to-day CS&D decisions are made directly by the Head of Customer Success & Delivery without routine COO involvement (see interviews and meeting records).
- **Systems accessed:** CRM, project system (read access).
- **Process participation:** P2, P8 (formal oversight; limited direct involvement observed).
- **Backup/delegate:** None named.

## Head of Sales — Diane Okafor

- **Function:** Sales
- **Reports to:** Renata Voss (CEO)
- **Responsibilities:** Sales strategy, team management, pipeline oversight, deal approvals within her authority.
- **Decision rights:** Approves Account Executive assignment, sales targets. Discount approval authority above 15% formally sits with the Head of Finance & People Ops, not Sales — see POL-01.
- **Systems accessed:** CRM (full access).
- **Process participation:** P1 (requester side), P8 (joint accountability with Head of CS&D — no documented tie-breaker).
- **Backup/delegate:** Callum Reyes (Senior Account Executive) informally covers for Diane on deal matters when she is unavailable; this is not a documented delegation.

## Senior Account Executive — Callum Reyes

- **Function:** Sales
- **Reports to:** Diane Okafor (Head of Sales)
- **Responsibilities:** Manage largest/most strategic accounts, mentor newer AEs.
- **Decision rights:** Standard AE discount authority below 15% (POL-01).
- **Systems accessed:** CRM.
- **Process participation:** P1, P8.

## Head of Customer Success & Delivery — Helena Cho

- **Function:** Customer Success & Delivery
- **Reports to:** Marcus Ihejirika (COO)
- **Responsibilities:** Onboarding delivery, support quality, renewal/churn-risk input, team management across Implementation and Support.
- **Decision rights:** Accountable for onboarding process (POL-03). No documented sole decision right over renewal terms — shared with Head of Sales (see PROC-07).
- **Systems accessed:** CRM, project system, support ticketing system.
- **Process participation:** P2, P5, P8.
- **Backup/delegate:** None named; several critical decisions (e.g. escalation-process changes) rest with her alone with no deputy identified.

## Support Lead — Sam Okonkwo

- **Function:** Customer Success & Delivery
- **Reports to:** Helena Cho (Head of Customer Success & Delivery)
- **Responsibilities:** Day-to-day support team management, ticket triage, escalation to Engineering.
- **Decision rights:** Accountable for ticket lifecycle under PROC-05. Proposed the draft v2 escalation revision (POL-04), which has not been formally approved.
- **Systems accessed:** Support ticketing system, CRM (read access).
- **Process participation:** P5.

## Head of Engineering — Lior Ben-David

- **Function:** Engineering & Product
- **Reports to:** Renata Voss (CEO)
- **Responsibilities:** Engineering delivery, technical architecture decisions, production deployment sign-off.
- **Decision rights:** Final say on technical feasibility for feature requests (see PROC-03; no single document states the Product/Engineering prioritisation split explicitly). **Production deployments touching customer billing require his sign-off** before release.
- **Systems accessed:** All engineering and production systems.
- **Process participation:** P3, P5 (engineering escalation), P7 (billing integration dependency).
- **Backup/delegate:** No named delegate for deployment sign-off.

## Product Managers — Grace Whitfield, Owen Mbeki

- **Function:** Engineering & Product
- **Reports to:** Lior Ben-David (Head of Engineering)
- **Responsibilities:** Feature request triage and prioritisation (PROC-03).
- **Decision rights:** Prioritisation call, per PROC-03. The two PMs split incoming requests informally; no documented rule for how product areas are divided between them.
- **Systems accessed:** Linear (current), CRM (read access).
- **Process participation:** P3.

## Senior Engineer — Ana Kowalski

- **Function:** Engineering & Product
- **Reports to:** Lior Ben-David (Head of Engineering)
- **Responsibilities:** Core platform engineering, including the legacy CRM-billing integration, which she built in 2021.
- **Decision rights:** None formally beyond standard engineer scope.
- **Systems accessed:** All engineering systems, billing integration (sole engineer with working production knowledge of this component).
- **Process participation:** P7 (billing integration), P5 (frequently pulled into Sev 1 incidents directly).
- **Backup/delegate:** None. No other engineer has made a production change to the billing integration in recent memory.

## QA Lead — Sofia Marchetti

- **Function:** Engineering & Product
- **Reports to:** Lior Ben-David (Head of Engineering)
- **Responsibilities:** Quality assurance across releases, data-quality checks.
- **Decision rights:** Not formally documented with respect to blocking a release. Her role description predates the current release process and does not address release-blocking authority.
- **Systems accessed:** Staging environment, CRM (read access), project system.
- **Process participation:** P3, general QA.

## Head of Finance & People Ops — Harriet Doyle

- **Function:** Finance & People Ops
- **Reports to:** Renata Voss (CEO)
- **Responsibilities:** Finance, expense approval, discount approval oversight, people operations oversight.
- **Decision rights:** Formal discount approval authority above 15% (POL-01), formal expense approval authority above $500 (POL-07).
- **Systems accessed:** CRM (approval fields), finance system, expenses spreadsheet.
- **Process participation:** P1, P4, P7.
- **Backup/delegate:** No named backup approver; in practice, Head of Sales exercises informal discount-approval authority in Harriet's absence or for urgent deals (undocumented).

## Financial Controller — Victor Adeyemi

- **Function:** Finance & People Ops
- **Reports to:** Harriet Doyle (Head of Finance & People Ops)
- **Responsibilities:** Day-to-day finance operations, invoicing, collections.
- **Decision rights:** Accountable for collections process (PROC-06). Named as discount approver in PROC-02, which has not been updated to match POL-01's current designation of the Head of Finance & People Ops as approver.
- **Systems accessed:** Finance system, CRM.
- **Process participation:** P1 (per outdated process doc), P7.

## People Ops Lead — Naomi Kessler

- **Function:** Finance & People Ops
- **Reports to:** Harriet Doyle (Head of Finance & People Ops)
- **Responsibilities:** New hire onboarding, probation decisions, HR administration.
- **Decision rights:** Sole approver of probation completion (POL-08).
- **Systems accessed:** HR system, project system (onboarding checklist tracking).
- **Process participation:** P6.

## Office & IT Ops Coordinator — Paul Vasquez

- **Function:** Finance & People Ops
- **Reports to:** Harriet Doyle (Head of Finance & People Ops)
- **Responsibilities:** IT systems administration, data-handling policy ownership.
- **Decision rights:** Owns POL-05. No document assigns him (or anyone else) responsibility for auditing expense-claim compliance, though this is sometimes assumed informally.
- **Systems accessed:** IT admin systems.
- **Process participation:** P4 (assumed but undocumented compliance-audit role).
text:
Role Descriptions and Decision Rights

Student-facing document. Part of Phase 1 release. Covers roles most relevant to the core processes; not every role in the roster has a full description. See decision_rights_table.md for a cross-role decision-rights summary.

CEO — Renata Voss

- Function: Leadership
- Reports to: Board
- Responsibilities: Overall strategy, board relationship, final call on strategic decisions (market expansion, fundraising).
- Decision rights: Sole authority on strategic direction; delegates day-to-day operational authority to the COO and function heads.
- Systems accessed: All systems (admin access).
- Process participation: P7 (strategic escalations only), general oversight.
- Backup/delegate: COO acts with delegated authority in the CEO's absence, except for strategic decisions.

COO — Marcus Ihejirika

- Function: Leadership
- Reports to: Renata Voss (CEO)
- Responsibilities: Operational oversight across Customer Success & Delivery, cross-functional coordination.
- Decision rights: Formal line management of Head of Customer Success & Delivery. In practice, day-to-day CS&D decisions are made directly by the Head of Customer Success & Delivery without routine COO involvement (see interviews and meeting records).
- Systems accessed: CRM, project system (read access).
- Process participation: P2, P8 (formal oversight; limited direct involvement observed).
- Backup/delegate: None named.

Head of Sales — Diane Okafor

- Function: Sales
- Reports to: Renata Voss (CEO)
- Responsibilities: Sales strategy, team management, pipeline oversight, deal approvals within her authority.
- Decision rights: Approves Account Executive assignment, sales targets. Discount approval authority above 15% formally sits with the Head of Finance & People Ops, not Sales — see POL-01.
- Systems accessed: CRM (full access).
- Process participation: P1 (requester side), P8 (joint accountability with Head of CS&D — no documented tie-breaker).
- Backup/delegate: Callum Reyes (Senior Account Executive) informally covers for Diane on deal matters when she is unavailable; this is not a documented delegation.

Senior Account Executive — Callum Reyes

- Function: Sales
- Reports to: Diane Okafor (Head of Sales)
- Responsibilities: Manage largest/most strategic accounts, mentor newer AEs.
- Decision rights: Standard AE discount authority below 15% (POL-01).
- Systems accessed: CRM.
- Process participation: P1, P8.

Head of Customer Success & Delivery — Helena Cho

- Function: Customer Success & Delivery
- Reports to: Marcus Ihejirika (COO)
- Responsibilities: Onboarding delivery, support quality, renewal/churn-risk input, team management across Implementation and Support.
- Decision rights: Accountable for onboarding process (POL-03). No documented sole decision right over renewal terms — shared with Head of Sales (see PROC-07).
- Systems accessed: CRM, project system, support ticketing system.
- Process participation: P2, P5, P8.
- Backup/delegate: None named; several critical decisions (e.g. escalation-process changes) rest with her alone with no deputy identified.

Support Lead — Sam Okonkwo

- Function: Customer Success & Delivery
- Reports to: Helena Cho (Head of Customer Success & Delivery)
- Responsibilities: Day-to-day support team management, ticket triage, escalation to Engineering.
- Decision rights: Accountable for ticket lifecycle under PROC-05. Proposed the draft v2 escalation revision (POL-04), which has not been formally approved.
- Systems accessed: Support ticketing system, CRM (read access).
- Process participation: P5.

Head of Engineering — Lior Ben-David

- Function: Engineering & Product
- Reports to: Renata Voss (CEO)
- Responsibilities: Engineering delivery, technical architecture decisions, production deployment sign-off.
- Decision rights: Final say on technical feasibility for feature requests (see PROC-03; no single document states the Product/Engineering prioritisation split explicitly). Production deployments touching customer billing require his sign-off before release.
- Systems accessed: All engineering and production systems.
- Process participation: P3, P5 (engineering escalation), P7 (billing integration dependency).
- Backup/delegate: No named delegate for deployment sign-off.

Product Managers — Grace Whitfield, Owen Mbeki

- Function: Engineering & Product
- Reports to: Lior Ben-David (Head of Engineering)
- Responsibilities: Feature request triage and prioritisation (PROC-03).
- Decision rights: Prioritisation call, per PROC-03. The two PMs split incoming requests informally; no documented rule for how product areas are divided between them.
- Systems accessed: Linear (current), CRM (read access).
- Process participation: P3.

Senior Engineer — Ana Kowalski

- Function: Engineering & Product
- Reports to: Lior Ben-David (Head of Engineering)
- Responsibilities: Core platform engineering, including the legacy CRM-billing integration, which she built in 2021.
- Decision rights: None formally beyond standard engineer scope.
- Systems accessed: All engineering systems, billing integration (sole engineer with working production knowledge of this component).
- Process participation: P7 (billing integration), P5 (frequently pulled into Sev 1 incidents directly).
- Backup/delegate: None. No other engineer has made a production change to the billing integration in recent memory.

QA Lead — Sofia Marchetti

- Function: Engineering & Product
- Reports to: Lior Ben-David (Head of Engineering)
- Responsibilities: Quality assurance across releases, data-quality checks.
- Decision rights: Not formally documented with respect to blocking a release. Her role description predates the current release process and does not address release-blocking authority.
- Systems accessed: Staging environment, CRM (read access), project system.
- Process participation: P3, general QA.

Head of Finance & People Ops — Harriet Doyle

- Function: Finance & People Ops
- Reports to: Renata Voss (CEO)
- Responsibilities: Finance, expense approval, discount approval oversight, people operations oversight.
- Decision rights: Formal discount approval authority above 15% (POL-01), formal expense approval authority above $500 (POL-07).
- Systems accessed: CRM (approval fields), finance system, expenses spreadsheet.
- Process participation: P1, P4, P7.
- Backup/delegate: No named backup approver; in practice, Head of Sales exercises informal discount-approval authority in Harriet's absence or for urgent deals (undocumented).

Financial Controller — Victor Adeyemi

- Function: Finance & People Ops
- Reports to: Harriet Doyle (Head of Finance & People Ops)
- Responsibilities: Day-to-day finance operations, invoicing, collections.
- Decision rights: Accountable for collections process (PROC-06). Named as discount approver in PROC-02, which has not been updated to match POL-01's current designation of the Head of Finance & People Ops as approver.
- Systems accessed: Finance system, CRM.
- Process participation: P1 (per outdated process doc), P7.

People Ops Lead — Naomi Kessler

- Function: Finance & People Ops
- Reports to: Harriet Doyle (Head of Finance & People Ops)
- Responsibilities: New hire onboarding, probation decisions, HR administration.
- Decision rights: Sole approver of probation completion (POL-08).
- Systems accessed: HR system, project system (onboarding checklist tracking).
- Process participation: P6.

- Reports to: Harriet Doyle (Head of Finance & People Ops)
- Responsibilities: IT systems administration, data-handling policy ownership.

text_raw:
# POL-01 — Discount Approval Policy

- **Document owner:** Harriet Doyle, Head of Finance & People Ops
- **Version:** 3.0
- **Approval status:** Approved
- **Effective date:** 2025-03-01
- **Review date:** 2026-09-01
- **Supersedes:** POL-02 (v2.1, effective 2021-06-01 – 2025-02-28)
- **Applicable to:** All employees with deal-closing authority (Sales function)
- **Related documents:** PROC-02 (Discount Approval Process), POL-06 (Contract Renewal Discount Policy)

## Purpose

To ensure discounts offered to customers are commercially sound and do not erode margin without appropriate oversight.

## Formal requirements

1. Any discount of **15% or greater** off list price on a new-business deal requires written approval from the Head of Finance & People Ops before the deal is marked Closed Won in the CRM.
2. Approval must be recorded in the CRM's `approval_record` field, referencing the approver and date.
3. Discounts below 15% may be approved by the deal's Account Executive without further sign-off.
4. This policy applies to new-business deals. Renewal discounting is governed separately by POL-06.

## Exceptions

None are formally documented under this version. Any deviation from the above requires an updated version of this policy.

## Version history

| Version | Effective | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 | 2020-03-01 | Initial policy, 10% threshold |
| 2.1 | 2021-06-01 | Clarified approval recording requirement |
| 3.0 | 2025-03-01 | Threshold raised from 10% to 15%, approved at leadership/finance meeting 2025-02-24 |

text_raw:
# POL-03 — Customer Onboarding & Implementation Policy

- **Document owner:** Helena Cho, Head of Customer Success & Delivery
- **Version:** 1.4
- **Approval status:** Approved
- **Effective date:** 2024-01-15
- **Review date:** 2026-01-15
- **Supersedes:** v1.0–1.3 (minor wording revisions only; no substantive change to timeline or ownership since v1.0)
- **Applicable to:** All new-business customer accounts
- **Related documents:** PROC-01 (Customer Onboarding & Implementation Process), PROC-06 (Invoicing & Collections Process)

## Purpose

To ensure new customers reach productive use of Northfield OS within a predictable timeframe, with clear ownership.

## Formal requirements

1. Every new-business account is assigned a named Implementation Specialist within 2 business days of contract signature.
2. Standard onboarding is completed within **6 weeks** of assignment.
3. The assigned Implementation Specialist is accountable for onboarding completion for their account, including coordinating any input required from Support or Engineering.
4. Onboarding is considered complete only when the account's onboarding checklist is marked complete in the project system.
5. Formal handover to the Support team must occur before an account is considered to be in standard support.

## Exceptions

Timeline extensions may be granted for accounts with unusual technical complexity. This policy does not specify who holds authority to approve such an extension.

## Background

Prior to this policy, onboarding was managed on an ad hoc basis by whichever Account Executive closed the deal, with no dedicated implementation role or standard timeline.

- **Document owner:** Sam Okonkwo, Support Lead

- **Approval status:** DRAFT — not approved; informal pilot proposed, see MTG-04.
- **Effective date:** Not yet in force

- **Applicable to:** Support Reps and Support Lead (Customer Success & Delivery); on-call Engineering staff, as the escalation counterparty
- **Related documents:** PROC-05 (Support Escalation Process, v1 — still the only approved version)

## Purpose (as drafted)

To revise the escalation path so that Severity 1 and 2 issues can be escalated directly to a named on-call engineer via Slack, rather than requiring a ticket to be raised first.

## Proposed requirements (NOT formally in force)

1. Severity 1 issues may be escalated directly to the on-call engineer via the `#eng-oncall` Slack channel. A ticket should be raised retrospectively within 24 hours.
2. Severity 2 issues continue to require a ticket before escalation, as under the current (v1) process.
3. Support Reps may close an escalated ticket once the customer confirms resolution, without requiring Engineering sign-off.

## Exceptions (as drafted)

None proposed beyond the Severity 1 Slack-escalation path itself, which departs from the standard ticket-first process described in PROC-05.

- **Review date:** 2025-05-01 (review overdue by more than a year as of period end)
- **Applicable to:** All employees with access to customer data

## Purpose

To set expectations for how employees handle customer data outside of Northfield's core systems.

## Formal requirements

1. Customer data should primarily be accessed and worked with inside approved systems (CRM, project system, Northfield OS admin console).
2. Where offline work is genuinely required, customer data **may be exported to a personal device for the purposes of offline work, provided it is deleted within 24 hours.**
3. Customer data must not be shared externally without the customer's consent.

## Exceptions

None documented.

title: POL-08 — New Hire Onboarding & Probation Policy
author: Naomi Kessler, People Ops Lead
text_raw:
# POL-08 — New Hire Onboarding & Probation Policy

- **Document owner:** Naomi Kessler, People Ops Lead
- **Version:** 1.3
- **Approval status:** Approved
- **Effective date:** 2021-05-24
- **Review date:** 2026-05-24
- **Applicable to:** All new employees
- **Related documents:** None formally linked.

## Purpose

To ensure new hires are set up consistently and that probation outcomes are decided by a single accountable role.

## Formal requirements

1. Every new hire completes a documented onboarding checklist (systems access, policy acknowledgement, role-specific training) within their **first two weeks**.
2. The People Ops Lead is the **sole approver** of a new hire's successful completion of probation, based on input from the hire's manager.
3. Probation period is 3 months from start date.

## Exceptions

This policy does not address onboarding for remote employees specifically; the checklist was written with an in-person office setup assumed.

## Background

Before this policy was introduced, new-hire onboarding was handled informally by whichever manager was doing the hiring, with no standard checklist and no single approver of probation outcomes.

# PROC-01 — Customer Onboarding & Implementation Process

- **Owner:** Helena Cho, Head of Customer Success & Delivery
- **Last updated:** 2024-01-20
- **Related policy:** POL-03

## Purpose

Take a newly signed customer from contract signature to productive use of Northfield OS within 6 weeks.

## Trigger

Deal marked "Closed Won" in CRM.

## Steps

1. **Assignment** (Day 0–2): Implementation Specialist assigned by Head of Customer Success & Delivery, based on current workload.
2. **Kickoff call** (Week 1): Specialist runs kickoff call with customer's nominated admin; confirms scope, systems access, data migration needs.
3. **Configuration** (Weeks 1–3): Specialist configures Northfield OS for customer's team structure, imports existing scheduling data.
4. **Training** (Weeks 3–4): Specialist runs live training sessions for customer's field staff and office admin.
5. **Go-live** (Week 5): Customer begins using Northfield OS for live scheduling.
6. **Handover to Support** (Week 6): Specialist marks onboarding complete in project system; account formally handed to the Support team via handover checklist.

## Responsible / Accountable

- **Responsible:** Assigned Implementation Specialist (all steps)
- **Accountable:** Head of Customer Success & Delivery

## Inputs

Signed contract, customer's existing data/spreadsheets (if migrating), CRM deal record.

## Outputs

Configured Northfield OS instance, trained customer users, completed onboarding checklist in project system, invoicing triggered.

## Systems used

CRM, project system, Northfield OS admin console.

## Required approvals

None specified for standard onboarding. Timeline extensions for complex accounts are handled case-by-case (no formal approval step documented).

## Expected timing

6 weeks, start to finish.

## Exceptions and escalation path

Not documented. In practice, onboarding-related technical issues are raised directly with Engineering rather than through a documented escalation step (see PROC-05 for the general escalation path).

title: PROC-02 — Discount Approval Process
author: Victor Adeyemi, Financial Controller
text_raw:
# PROC-02 — Discount Approval Process

- **Owner:** Victor Adeyemi, Financial Controller
- **Last updated:** 2022-08-15
- **Related policy:** POL-01

## Purpose

Ensure discounts above the approval threshold are reviewed before a deal closes.

## Trigger

Account Executive prepares a deal with a discount at or above the policy threshold.

## Steps

1. Account Executive flags the deal as requiring approval in the CRM.
2. Account Executive submits discount rationale (competitive pressure, deal size, strategic account, etc.) to the Financial Controller.
3. **Financial Controller reviews and approves or rejects the discount**, recording the decision in the CRM `approval_record` field.
4. If approved, Account Executive proceeds to close the deal.
5. If rejected, Account Executive renegotiates terms with the customer.

## Responsible / Accountable

- **Responsible:** Account Executive (steps 1, 2, 4/5)
- **Accountable:** Financial Controller (step 3)

## Inputs

CRM deal record, discount rationale.

## Outputs

Recorded approval/rejection decision.

## Systems used

CRM.

## Required approvals

Financial Controller sign-off (per this document).

## Expected timing

1 business day.

## Exceptions and escalation path

Not documented.

text_raw:
# PROC-03 — Product Change / Feature Request Intake Process

- **Owner:** Grace Whitfield, Product Manager
- **Last updated:** 2023-11-02
- **Related policy:** None formal.

## Purpose

Capture, triage and prioritise feature and product change requests from customers, Support and internal stakeholders.

## Trigger

Any stakeholder identifies a desired product change.

## Steps

1. Requester adds a card to the **Feature Requests Trello board**, tagging the relevant customer(s) if applicable.
2. Product Manager reviews new cards weekly and tags each with a priority (P1–P4).
3. Product Manager and Head of Engineering jointly review P1 cards in the weekly product-eng sync.
4. Approved cards are moved to the "Planned" column and assigned to an engineering sprint.
5. Requester is notified when their request ships.

## Responsible / Accountable

- **Responsible:** Requester (step 1), Product Manager (steps 2, 5)
- **Accountable:** Product Manager (prioritisation), Head of Engineering (feasibility/sequencing)

## Inputs

Customer feedback, Support tickets, internal ideas.

## Outputs

Prioritised, planned feature work.

## Systems used

Trello.

## Required approvals

Head of Engineering sign-off for P1 cards entering a sprint.

## Expected timing

Weekly triage cycle.

## Exceptions and escalation path

Not documented.

# PROC-04 — Expense Approval Process

- **Owner:** Harriet Doyle, Head of Finance & People Ops
- **Last updated:** 2021-09-10
- **Related policy:** POL-07

## Purpose

Review and approve employee expense claims prior to reimbursement.

## Trigger

Employee submits an expense claim with receipt(s).

## Steps

1. Employee submits claim via the shared expenses spreadsheet, attaching receipts.
2. If claim is $500 or under, employee's direct manager reviews and approves.
3. If claim is over $500, claim is routed to the Head of Finance & People Ops for approval.
4. Approved claims are processed for reimbursement in the next pay cycle.

## Responsible / Accountable

- **Responsible:** Employee (step 1), direct manager or Head of Finance & People Ops (approval step)
- **Accountable:** Head of Finance & People Ops

## Inputs

Expense claim, itemised receipts.

## Outputs

Approved/rejected claim, reimbursement.

## Systems used

Shared expenses spreadsheet.

## Required approvals

Per POL-07 thresholds.

## Expected timing

Within the same pay cycle the claim is submitted, where submitted before the monthly cutoff.

## Exceptions and escalation path

Not documented. (Travel expenses incurred during customer onboarding visits are treated by Finance as standing pre-approved in practice, but this exception does not appear in this process document or in POL-07.)

text_raw:
# PROC-05 — Support Escalation Process (v1 — approved)

- **Owner:** Sam Okonkwo, Support Lead
- **Last updated:** 2021-02-10
- **Approval status:** Approved. This is the current formally approved version. (See POL-04 for an unapproved draft revision.)

## Purpose

Ensure customer-reported issues that Support cannot resolve are escalated to Engineering consistently.

## Trigger

Support Rep cannot resolve a customer-reported issue within their access/knowledge.

## Steps

1. Support Rep classifies severity (Sev 1–3) based on customer impact.
2. Support Rep raises a ticket in the support system, tagging severity and affected system.
3. Support Lead reviews Sev 1 tickets immediately; Sev 2/3 tickets at next triage.
4. Ticket assigned to an engineer by the Head of Engineering (or delegate).
5. Engineer investigates, resolves or escalates further, and updates the ticket.
6. Support Lead confirms resolution with the customer and closes the ticket.

## Responsible / Accountable

- **Responsible:** Support Rep (steps 1–2), assigned Engineer (step 5)
- **Accountable:** Support Lead (ticket lifecycle), Head of Engineering (engineering assignment)

## Inputs

Customer report, product/system knowledge.

## Outputs

Resolved ticket, customer communication.

## Systems used

Support ticketing system, Slack (internal coordination only).

## Required approvals

None for standard resolution; Support Lead confirms closure.

## Expected timing

Sev 1: same business day. Sev 2: 2 business days. Sev 3: 5 business days.

## Exceptions and escalation path

None documented for bypassing the ticket step. In practice, Sev 1 production issues are frequently raised directly with an engineer via Slack before or instead of a ticket being created.

title: PROC-06 — Invoicing & Collections Process
author: Victor Adeyemi, Financial Controller
text_raw:
# PROC-06 — Invoicing & Collections Process

- **Owner:** Victor Adeyemi, Financial Controller
- **Last updated:** 2022-11-01
- **Related policy:** None formal; operates alongside POL-03.

## Purpose

Ensure customers are invoiced accurately and promptly, and overdue invoices are followed up.

## Trigger

CRM deal marked "Closed Won" AND linked onboarding project marked complete in the project system.

## Steps

1. Billing integration automatically generates an invoice in Northfield's finance system once both trigger conditions are met.
2. Invoice sent to customer's billing contact.
3. Financial Controller reviews payment status weekly.
4. If an invoice is overdue by 15 days, an automated reminder is sent.
5. If overdue by 30 days, Financial Controller personally contacts the customer.
6. If overdue by 45 days, Financial Controller escalates to the Head of Finance & People Ops for a decision on further action (late fee, account hold, or write-off).

## Responsible / Accountable

- **Responsible:** Financial Controller (steps 3–6), billing integration (steps 1–2, automated)
- **Accountable:** Financial Controller

## Inputs

CRM deal status, onboarding completion status, contract terms.

## Outputs

Issued invoice, payment record, collections escalation where relevant.

## Systems used

CRM, project system, Northfield finance system, billing integration between Northfield OS and CRM.

## Required approvals

Head of Finance & People Ops decision required at the 45-day escalation point.

## Expected timing

Invoice generated within 1 business day of both trigger conditions being met.

## Exceptions and escalation path

The 45-day escalation path is the only documented exception path.

text_raw:
# PROC-07 — Contract Renewal & Churn-Risk Review Process

- **Owner:** Jointly maintained by Sales and Customer Success & Delivery
- **Last updated:** 2024-07-05
- **Related policy:** POL-06

## Purpose

Identify accounts at risk of not renewing, and manage the renewal negotiation process.

## Trigger

Account reaches 90 days before contract end date, OR Customer Success flags an account as churn-risk based on usage/engagement signals.

## Steps

1. Customer Success reviews account health quarterly and flags at-risk accounts.
2. Flagged accounts are discussed at the joint Sales/CS renewal review meeting.
3. Account Executive leads commercial renewal conversation with the customer.
4. Customer Success provides relationship-health input to the Account Executive during negotiation.
5. Renewal terms (including any discount, per POL-06) are agreed and the contract is renewed or the account churns.

## Responsible / Accountable

- **Responsible:** Customer Success (flagging, relationship input), Account Executive (commercial negotiation)
- **Accountable:** Not specified — see Exceptions.

## Inputs

Account usage data, contract terms, relationship history.

## Outputs

Renewed contract or confirmed churn.

## Systems used

CRM, Northfield OS usage analytics (informal review, not a defined dashboard).

## Required approvals

Discount terms per POL-06. No approval step specified for the renewal decision itself.

## Expected timing

Review cycle begins 90 days before contract end date.

## Exceptions and escalation path

Not documented. Both the Head of Sales and Head of Customer Success & Delivery have historically signed off on renewal strategy for at-risk accounts, but no escalation path exists for cases where they disagree on approach or discount terms.

# INT-01 — Interview: Renata Voss

- **Role / function:** CEO / Founder, Leadership
- **Tenure:** 6.5 years (founder)
- **Interview date:** 2026-06-22
- **Areas of responsibility:** Overall strategy, board relationship, final say on strategic decisions.

## Processes performed directly

Strategic decision-making, board reporting. Not involved in day-to-day operation of any of the eight core processes.

Everything operational — relies on function heads for detail.

On day-to-day discount approvals: *"That's Harriet and Diane's world, honestly. I trust them to sort it out between them."*

None described directly — states she would expect function heads to raise anything of concern to her, but acknowledges she "wouldn't necessarily hear about smaller workarounds."

## Statements of uncertainty

Explicit throughout regarding operational detail; confident only on strategic-level statements.

## References

Harriet Doyle, Diane Okafor, Marcus Ihejirika; MTG-06 (leadership meeting on cleaning-vertical expansion).

# INT-02 — Interview: Diane Okafor

- **Role / function:** Head of Sales, Sales
- **Tenure:** 5.1 years
- **Interview date:** 2026-06-15
- **Areas of responsibility:** Sales strategy, team management, pipeline, deal approvals within her authority.

## Processes performed directly

P1 (discount approval, requester/manager side), P8 (renewal, commercial ownership).

## Processes only observed or heard about

P4 (expense approval) — aware only that "Finance handles it."

## Discussion notes

On discount approval: *"Anything over 15% goes to Harriet. That's been the rule since we bumped the threshold last year. My team knows it and we're pretty disciplined about it — I'd be surprised if there were deals slipping through without sign-off."*

On urgent deals: *"Look, if something's time-sensitive and Harriet's not around, I'll just tell the AE to go ahead and I'll square it with her after. That's not really bypassing anything, it's just being pragmatic — we're a small company."*

On renewals: *"AEs own the commercial conversation on renewal, CS gives us the read on relationship health. That's how it's always worked."*

## Exceptions and workarounds

The "square it with Harriet after" workaround described above.

## Statements of uncertainty

None on discount policy (high confidence). More measured on the renewal decision-rights question: *"Helena and I usually land in the same place. The Ridgeway renewal's about the closest we've come to actually disagreeing, and even then it felt more like we were still talking it through than genuinely stuck."*

## References

Harriet Doyle, Callum Reyes, Helena Cho; POL-01; MTG-05.

## Processes only observed or heard about

P2, P3 — aware only at a summary level.

## Discussion notes

On discount approval: *"I approve what comes to me. I know Diane sometimes okays urgent ones herself and tells me after — that's not really how the policy reads, but I get why it happens. I'll be straight with you, I don't have full visibility into how often it happens versus how often it's reported to me."*

On travel expenses: *"We don't make onboarding folks get sign-off for every flight and hotel on a customer visit — that would be ridiculous admin for something we've basically already decided is fine. It's not written down anywhere, it's just how we operate."*

On the June review: *"We flagged at the quarterly review that some managers are pre-approving expenses themselves instead of sending them to me. We said we'd look at updating the policy next quarter. Nothing's actually changed yet — it's on the list."*

## Exceptions and workarounds

Travel expense standing exception (undocumented); awareness of informal manager pre-approval for expenses.

## Statements of uncertainty

Candid that her own visibility into how often the informal discount workaround happens is incomplete, and stops short of saying the expense-policy gap has actually been fixed rather than just flagged.

Diane Okafor; POL-01, POL-07; MTG-09.

Processes performed directly

P1 (discount approval, formal), P4 (expense approval, formal), P7 (escalation decisions).

Processes only observed or heard about

P2, P3 — aware only at a summary level.

Discussion notes

On discount approval: "I approve what comes to me. I know Diane sometimes okays urgent ones herself and tells me after — that's not really how the policy reads, but I get why it happens. I'll be straight with you, I don't have full visibility into how often it happens versus how often it's reported to me."

On travel expenses: "We don't make onboarding folks get sign-off for every flight and hotel on a customer visit — that would be ridiculous admin for something we've basically already decided is fine. It's not written down anywhere, it's just how we operate."

Travel expense standing exception (undocumented); awareness of informal manager pre-approval for expenses.

Candid that her own visibility into how often the informal discount workaround happens is incomplete, and stops short of saying the expense-policy gap has actually been fixed rather than just flagged.

author: Adaeze Nwosu
text_raw:
# INT-06 — Interview: Adaeze Nwosu

- **Role / function:** Implementation Specialist, Customer Success & Delivery
- **Tenure:** 4.2 years
- **Interview date:** 2026-06-19
- **Areas of responsibility:** Customer onboarding for assigned accounts.

## Processes performed directly

P2 (onboarding, full lifecycle), informal support of P5 during onboarding-adjacent issues.

## Processes only observed or heard about

P1, P4, P7, P8 — aware only peripherally.

## Discussion notes

On the onboarding process: *"Kickoff in week one, config and training over the next few weeks, go-live around week five, and then we hand off to Support in week six. That's basically always how it runs — no idea why six weeks specifically, that's just always been the number since before I joined."*

On onboarding effort not captured in the system: *"A good chunk of my week is just emailing customers back and forth, sorting out little things — none of that shows up as a task. If someone only looked at the project system they'd think onboarding takes way less effort than it does."*

On supporting newer colleagues: *"Ruth's still fairly new — I've walked her through a few onboardings that weren't quite textbook. I know at least once she was working off an older version of our checklist that one of the other Specialists had saved locally; I told her to use the current one, but I don't know how she originally got the old one."*

On travel: *"Nobody makes us get separate sign-off for onboarding-visit travel, we just book it. It's not written down that I know of, it's just accepted."*

On timeline extensions: *"If an account's more complex we might run a bit longer than six weeks. I've just always cleared that with Helena informally — I couldn't point you to anything that says it has to be her specifically."*

## Exceptions and workarounds

Timeline extensions handled informally; some onboarding effort untracked in the project system; outdated checklist circulating informally.

## Statements of uncertainty

Explicit on the "why six weeks" question and on whether Helena's sign-off is a formal requirement or just her own habit.

## References

Ruth Padgett, Helena Cho; PROC-01.

# INT-07 — Interview: Sam Okonkwo

## Processes performed directly

P5 (escalation, full lifecycle).

## Processes only observed or heard about

P2, P8 — limited.

On the escalation process: *"We classify severity, raise a ticket, and if it's a Sev 1 I get an engineer on it straight away. For anything urgent in production, we usually just grab someone on Slack directly rather than waiting on the ticket queue — the ticket gets filled in properly afterwards."*

Slack-direct escalation for Sev 1 production issues.

None volunteered on the approval-status question — he spoke about "the new version" being approved with the same flat confidence as everything else he said, without qualifying how or when that approval actually happened.

## References

Helena Cho; POL-04; PROC-05; Ines Torres, Deshawn Riley.

# INT-10 — Interview: Ana Kowalski

- **Role / function:** Senior Engineer, Engineering & Product
- **Tenure:** 6.0 years
- **Interview date:** 2026-06-23
- **Areas of responsibility:** Core platform engineering; sole owner of the legacy CRM-billing integration.

## Processes performed directly

P7 (billing integration maintenance), P5 (frequently pulled into Sev 1 incidents), P3 (occasional feasibility input).

## Processes only observed or heard about

P1, P2, P4 — no direct involvement.

## Discussion notes

On the billing integration: *"I built that integration back in 2021 and I'm still the only one who really understands how it talks to the CRM — nobody else has touched the production code for it since. It's held up fine day to day, but it's obviously a risk if I'm not around."*

On the February 2026 incident: *"The integration broke during a CRM update in February and stopped reconciling invoice status properly for about two days. We said afterwards we'd get proper documentation written up so it wasn't just in my head — Femi was going to lead that. Last I checked, it still hasn't happened. Not for any bad reason, just other things kept taking priority."*

On being pulled into incidents: *"During that incident people were messaging me directly rather than going through a ticket first — which makes sense given the urgency, but it does mean there's not always a clean paper trail of exactly what I changed and when, versus what showed up properly in the ticket afterwards."*

On feature intake: *"We've been in Linear for over a year now, not Trello — I think the last time I saw the old process doc it still mentioned Trello, which made me raise an eyebrow, but nobody's gotten around to updating it."*

On Product/Engineering prioritisation: *"Grace and Owen basically just divide up requests between them by who has bandwidth or knows the customer, there's no strict rule I've seen. As for who has the final say between Product and Engineering when we disagree on something — I genuinely don't know that there's ever been a clean answer to that. It just gets talked out."*

## Exceptions and workarounds

Sole-owner risk on billing integration; direct Slack escalation during incidents; unmet documentation commitment.

## Statements of uncertainty

Explicit on the Product/Engineering decision-rights question.

## References

Femi Adekunle; Grace Whitfield, Owen Mbeki; MTG-07.

text_raw:
# MTG-01 — Discount Policy Review

- **Date:** 2025-02-24
- **Participants:** Renata Voss (CEO), Harriet Doyle (Head of Finance & People Ops), Diane Okafor (Head of Sales)
- **Purpose:** Review whether the 10% discount approval threshold is still appropriate given deal-size trends.

## Discussion

Harriet presented data showing that a growing share of deals were being flagged for approval at the 10% threshold, adding review burden without changing outcomes (almost all were approved). Diane argued the threshold was out of step with typical enterprise-software discounting norms and was slowing deals down unnecessarily. Renata asked whether raising the threshold created margin risk; Harriet said modelling suggested minimal impact given historical discount patterns clustered below 15%.

## Options considered

1. Keep threshold at 10%.
2. Raise threshold to 15%.
3. Raise threshold to 20%.

## Final decision

Raise the Finance approval threshold from 10% to 15%, effective 2025-03-01. Option 3 (20%) was discussed but not adopted — Harriet felt it removed too much oversight.

## Decision owner

Harriet Doyle (policy owner), with Renata Voss's sign-off.

## Rationale

Reduce approval overhead on low-risk deals while retaining oversight on larger discounts.

## Conditions or exceptions

None discussed or agreed.

## Actions

- Harriet Doyle to update and circulate POL-01 by 2025-03-01. (Done — see POL-01.)
- Diane Okafor to brief the Sales team on the new threshold.

## Unresolved matters

None recorded at the time.

# MTG-02 — Sales Team Weekly

- **Date:** 2025-06-12
- **Participants:** Diane Okafor (Head of Sales), Callum Reyes, Priya Anand, Jonah Fischer, Ester Malik, Tomas Bright (all Sales)
- **Purpose:** Regular weekly pipeline review. Item raised informally: handling of a time-sensitive deal awaiting discount approval.

## Discussion

Priya raised that a deal was stuck because Harriet Doyle was on leave and the customer needed an answer within 48 hours. Diane said: *"For now, if it's genuinely urgent and I'm comfortable with it, just get my sign-off directly and we'll sort the paperwork out properly after — I don't want us losing deals over an admin gap. We'll fix the process properly later."* No formal vote or decision process followed; this was said in the context of a routine team meeting, not a policy review.

## Options considered

Priya's stuck deal was the only option on the table when Diane responded — there wasn't a broader options discussion.

## Final decision

Diane's statement above stands as the only record of what was agreed: get her sign-off directly on genuinely urgent deals while Harriet's out, sort the CRM entry out afterwards.

## Decision owner

Diane Okafor. Not made jointly with Harriet Doyle or Renata Voss.

## Rationale

Avoid losing time-sensitive deals due to an approver's temporary unavailability.

## Conditions or exceptions

Framed by Diane as temporary ("for now") and pending a proper process fix ("we'll fix the process properly later").

## Actions

- No action item was formally logged for "fixing the process properly."

## Unresolved matters

Whether/when this temporary accommodation would be formalised, reviewed, or withdrawn was never revisited in any subsequent meeting on record.

# MTG-03 — Product/Engineering Planning

- **Date:** 2025-04-22
- **Participants:** Lior Ben-David (Head of Engineering), Grace Whitfield (Product Manager), Owen Mbeki (Product Manager), Ana Kowalski (Senior Engineer)
- **Purpose:** Address growing complaints that the Trello feature-request board was hard to search and didn't integrate with sprint planning.

## Discussion

Grace proposed migrating feature-request tracking to Linear, which the engineering team already used for sprint planning, to reduce duplicate tooling. Lior supported this; Ana noted it would simplify linking feature requests to engineering tickets directly. Owen raised that historical Trello cards would need to be manually re-entered or archived, which would take some cleanup time.

## Options considered

text_raw:
# MTG-04 — Customer Success & Delivery Team Meeting

- **Date:** 2025-09-09
- **Participants:** Helena Cho (Head of Customer Success & Delivery), Sam Okonkwo (Support Lead), Ines Torres, Deshawn Riley (Support Reps)
- **Purpose:** Discuss proposed revisions to the support escalation process.

## Discussion

Sam presented a draft revision (subsequently circulated as POL-04 v2) allowing direct Slack escalation to an on-call engineer for Sev 1 issues, and allowing reps to close tickets themselves once a customer confirms resolution, without requiring Engineering sign-off. Sam argued the current ticket-first requirement was adding delay during production incidents when engineers were often being contacted directly anyway. Helena was broadly supportive but cautious about formalising a process change without more data.

Helena: *"I like the direction. Let's pilot it informally for a quarter — don't roll it out as official yet, just see how it goes — and then we'll look at formally updating the process document if it's working."*

## Options considered

1. Keep current (v1) process as-is.
2. Approve v2 immediately as the new standard.
3. Pilot v2 informally for one quarter before deciding.

## Final decision

Option 3 — an informal quarter-long pilot, rather than formal approval of the revised process document (POL-04).

## Decision owner

Helena Cho.

## Rationale

Test the revised approach before committing to a formal process change.

## Conditions or exceptions

Explicitly framed as a pilot, not a policy change. Helena did not set a specific date to review the pilot outcome or decide on formal approval.

## Actions

- Sam Okonkwo to run the pilot with his team starting immediately.
- No action item was created for Helena (or anyone) to formally review the pilot at the end of the quarter.

## Unresolved matters

The pilot review Helena mentioned doesn't appear to have happened. POL-04 is still sitting in draft, even though Sam's team has been running on it since September 2025.

title: MTG-05 — Quarterly Renewal & Churn-Risk Review
author: Diane Okafor (Head of Sales), Helena Cho (Head of Customer Success & Delivery), Callum Reyes (Senior Account Executive)

metadata.participants: Diane Okafor (Head of Sales), Helena Cho (Head of Customer Success & Delivery), Callum Reyes (Senior Account Executive)
metadata.purpose: Review accounts approaching renewal and identify churn-risk accounts requiring proactive outreach.

text_raw:
# MTG-05 — Quarterly Renewal & Churn-Risk Review

- **Date:** 2025-11-14
- **Participants:** Diane Okafor (Head of Sales), Helena Cho (Head of Customer Success & Delivery), Callum Reyes (Senior Account Executive)
- **Purpose:** Review accounts approaching renewal and identify churn-risk accounts requiring proactive outreach.

## Discussion

Helena presented usage data flagging four accounts as churn-risk based on declining login activity. The group agreed these should receive proactive outreach within 30 days. Discussion then turned to a specific enterprise account (referred to in this meeting as the "Ridgeway account") approaching contract end, where Callum (account owner) wanted to offer a discount above the 10% renewal cap to secure the renewal, citing competitive pressure from a rival vendor. Helena pushed back, arguing the relationship was strong enough that a large discount wasn't necessary and would set a bad precedent. Diane and Helena did not reach agreement on the discount level during the meeting.

Diane: *"I hear you, but ultimately if it's my rep's account and my number to hit, I think that's a sales call."*
Helena: *"I'm not saying it isn't, I just want it on record that I don't think it's necessary here."*

## Options considered

1. Offer the Ridgeway account a renewal discount above 10% to secure the deal.
2. Hold firm at the 10% cap and risk losing the account.
3. Delay the decision pending further customer conversation.

## Final decision

No decision was reached in this meeting. The group agreed to "keep talking to the customer" without committing to a discount figure. Neither Diane nor Helena deferred to the other, and no one else at the meeting had authority to break the tie.

## Decision owner

Not established. Neither role has documented final authority over renewal discount decisions when Sales and Customer Success disagree (see PROC-07).

## Rationale

N/A — no decision made.

## Conditions or exceptions

N/A.

## Actions

- Helena Cho and CS team to begin proactive outreach to the four flagged churn-risk accounts within 30 days.
- Callum Reyes to continue the Ridgeway conversation and report back. No due date was set for a final resolution.

## Unresolved matters

- The Ridgeway account's renewal discount was not resolved in this meeting or, as far as the available records show, subsequently — its contract end date passed without a formal extension or renewal being executed.
- No mechanism exists for resolving disagreements between Sales and Customer Success on renewal terms.

title: MTG-06 — Leadership Strategy Session
author: Renata Voss (CEO), Marcus Ihejirika (COO), Diane Okafor (Head of Sales), Lior Ben-David (Head of Engineering), Harriet Doyle (Head of Finance & People Ops)

metadata.participants: Renata Voss (CEO), Marcus Ihejirika (COO), Diane Okafor (Head of Sales), Lior Ben-David (Head of Engineering), Harriet Doyle (Head of Finance & People Ops)
metadata.purpose: Review progress on evaluating expansion into the commercial cleaning services vertical (a market-adjacency exploration started in mid-2025).

text_raw:
# MTG-06 — Leadership Strategy Session

- **Date:** 2026-01-20
- **Participants:** Renata Voss (CEO), Marcus Ihejirika (COO), Diane Okafor (Head of Sales), Lior Ben-David (Head of Engineering), Harriet Doyle (Head of Finance & People Ops)
- **Purpose:** Review progress on evaluating expansion into the commercial cleaning services vertical (a market-adjacency exploration started in mid-2025).

## Discussion

Diane presented early customer discovery findings from conversations with cleaning-services businesses: interest existed but sales cycles looked longer and the compliance-tracking features needed differed meaningfully from the trades-focused product. Lior flagged that supporting the vertical properly would likely require a dedicated engineering workstream, competing with the current roadmap. Renata noted the company did not currently have bandwidth to run two go-to-market motions in parallel.

Renata: *"I don't think we say never to this, but I don't think now is the moment either. Let's park it — not kill it, just park it — and revisit if the trades pipeline slows down or if we get a clear inbound signal from the cleaning side."*

## Options considered

1. Proceed with a dedicated cleaning-vertical go-to-market effort in 2026.
2. Pause the exploration indefinitely.
3. Pause the exploration with no defined trigger to revisit.

## Final decision

Pause the cleaning-vertical exploration. Renata mentioned a loose trigger for revisiting it verbally, but nothing more specific than that was written down anywhere.

## Decision owner

Renata Voss (CEO).

## Rationale

Limited bandwidth to run two go-to-market motions simultaneously; deprioritise the less mature opportunity.

## Conditions or exceptions

Renata's verbal framing ("revisit if the trades pipeline slows down or if we get a clear inbound signal") was not translated into any tracked metric, owner, or review date.

## Actions

- Diane Okafor to file discovery notes (informal, not distributed beyond this group as far as records show).
- No one was assigned to monitor for the "revisit" trigger Renata described.

## Unresolved matters

No later leadership meeting record revisited this decision.

text_raw:
# MTG-07 — Billing Integration Incident Review

- **Date:** 2026-02-18
- **Participants:** Lior Ben-David (Head of Engineering), Ana Kowalski (Senior Engineer), Femi Adekunle (Engineer), Sofia Marchetti (QA Lead)
- **Purpose:** Post-incident review of a billing-integration failure that stopped invoice/CRM reconciliation for approximately two days (2026-02-16 to 2026-02-18).

## Discussion

Ana walked through the timeline: a CRM configuration update on 2026-02-16 had an unanticipated interaction with the legacy billing integration, causing invoice status to stop syncing correctly with CRM deal records. She was contacted directly via Slack by Support once customers began reporting stale invoice statuses, rather than via a ticket being raised first, given the urgency. Ana diagnosed and fixed the issue by 2026-02-18. Sofia noted this was the second time in the integration's history that a change elsewhere in the system had unexpectedly affected it, and raised concern about the single-person dependency on Ana for this component.

Lior: *"We can't keep having this be a single point of failure. Femi, can you pair with Ana and get proper documentation written up on how this thing actually works, so it's not just in her head?"*
Femi: *"Yep, happy to — I'll block out time next sprint."*

## Options considered

1. Do nothing differently; treat this as a one-off.
2. Document the integration properly, with Femi leading.
3. Rebuild the integration from scratch to remove the dependency on legacy knowledge.

## Final decision

Option 2 — produce documentation, led by Femi Adekunle with Ana Kowalski's input.

## Decision owner

Lior Ben-David.

## Rationale

Reduce single-person dependency risk without the cost of a full rebuild.

## Conditions or exceptions

None specified regarding priority relative to other engineering work — "next sprint" was not formally scheduled or tracked as a committed deliverable.

## Actions

- Femi Adekunle to pair with Ana Kowalski and produce documentation. **Due:** "next sprint" (no specific date recorded).

## Unresolved matters

No corresponding documentation task was recorded as completed, and no follow-up review of this action item appears in any later meeting record.

# MTG-08 — Departure Handover Planning

- **Date:** 2026-04-25
- **Participants:** Lior Ben-David (Head of Engineering), Wei Zhang (Engineer, departing), Colm Brennan (Engineer)
- **Purpose:** Plan handover of Wei Zhang's responsibilities ahead of his last day (2026-04-30).

## Discussion

Wei listed his current areas of ownership: two customer-facing feature modules, a data-export tool used occasionally by Support, and some peripheral involvement in billing-integration testing (though not core maintenance, which remains Ana Kowalski's). Colm agreed to take over the two feature modules and the data-export tool. Time was limited (five business days remained), and the group agreed to prioritise the customer-facing items over documentation of the billing-integration testing work, on the basis that it was "lower risk."

Lior: *"Let's make sure the stuff customers can see is covered first. The billing testing notes — if we don't get to a full write-up, at least leave whatever you've got, even if it's messy."*

## Options considered

1. Full documented handover across all of Wei's work areas before departure.
2. Prioritise customer-facing work; accept a lighter, informal handover on lower-priority items.

## Final decision

Option 2.

## Decision owner

Lior Ben-David.

## Rationale

Limited time before departure; triage by customer impact.

## Conditions or exceptions

Billing-integration testing notes handover explicitly de-scoped to "whatever you've got, even if it's messy."

## Actions

- Colm Brennan to take over the two feature modules and data-export tool by 2026-04-30.
- Wei Zhang to leave any available notes on billing-integration testing before departure. No specific format or completeness bar was set.

## Unresolved matters

Whether adequate billing-integration testing notes were actually left was never confirmed in any available record.

text_raw:
# MTG-09 — Quarterly Finance & Ops Review

- **Date:** 2026-06-03
- **Participants:** Harriet Doyle (Head of Finance & People Ops), Victor Adeyemi (Financial Controller), Naomi Kessler (People Ops Lead)
- **Purpose:** Standing quarterly review of finance and operations matters.

## Discussion

Victor raised that several expense claims over the past quarter appeared to have been approved directly by managers rather than routed to Harriet, despite being under the informal understanding that manager approval only applied at or below $500. He cited two or three examples without pulling exact figures in the meeting. Harriet acknowledged this was a known pattern and said it hadn't caused any material issue so far, but agreed the policy or process should probably be tightened up, or at least clarified, so it was less ambiguous in practice. No specific changes were drafted in the meeting itself.

Harriet: *"Let's flag it for next quarter — I don't think we need to overreact, but I do want to look at whether the policy needs tightening or whether we just need to remind people how it's supposed to work."*

## Options considered

1. Leave as-is; treat as low-risk.
2. Update POL-07/PROC-04 to close the gap.
3. Reissue guidance reminding managers of the existing threshold, without changing the policy itself.

## Final decision

Deferred — flagged for the next quarterly review, targeted for September 2026. No option was selected.

## Decision owner

Harriet Doyle (as the deferral owner; no substantive decision made).

## Rationale

Considered low urgency; wanted more data before acting.

## Conditions or exceptions

None decided.

## Actions

- Victor Adeyemi to compile specific examples of manager-approved expenses over $500 ahead of the September review. No interim action taken.

## Unresolved matters

The underlying gap (managers informally pre-approving expenses above the documented threshold) remained open as of this meeting.

---

*A brief written summary of this meeting was circulated afterward to the wider Finance & People Ops function. That summary stated: "the team reviewed expense processes and confirmed things are working well."*

text_raw:
# MTG-10 — Ashgrove Trades Renewal Review

- **Date:** 2026-07-20
- **Participants:** Diane Okafor (Head of Sales), Helena Cho (Head of Customer Success & Delivery), Ruth Padgett (Implementation Specialist, account contact)
- **Purpose:** Finalise renewal terms for Ashgrove Trades ahead of its contract end date.

## Discussion

Ruth flagged that, in an earlier check-in call with the customer (not otherwise documented), she had told them informally that the renewal would "probably look similar to last time, around 10%" — a figure she'd never confirmed with Diane or Helena, just a reasonable guess based on the account's history. Diane said that assumption was now out of date: a competitor had recently approached Ashgrove Trades with an aggressive offer, and Diane wanted to secure a multi-year renewal before that went further. Helena agreed the relationship was strong enough to justify a modest increase in discount to lock in the term.

Diane: *"Ruth's 10% guess made sense at the time, but that's not where we should land now — I'd rather go to 12% and get two years locked in than hold the line and risk losing them to a competitive approach."*
Helena: *"Agreed. Let's make sure Ruth goes back to the customer with the actual number, not the placeholder one."*

## Options considered

1. Offer a one-year renewal at the previously-assumed ~10%, buying time before committing to anything longer.
2. Offer 12% in exchange for a two-year term.
3. Match the competitor's offer directly rather than counter with a round number.

## Final decision
